framework: Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 11 & Schedule III, Table Sl. No. 11) read with rule 279 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026
sourceTitle: Income-tax Rules, 2026 — rule 279 (limits for Schedule III, Table Sl. No. 11)
notes: From tax year 2026-27 the exempt HRA is the least of (1) actual HRA received, (2) rent paid minus 10% of salary, (3) 50% of salary in Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad and Bengaluru, or 40% elsewhere (rule 279). Section 202(2)(a)(i) removes the exemption under the default new regime. FY 2025-26 stays under section 10(13A) and Rule 2A of the 1961 law, where only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai got 50%.
assumptions: Taxpayer is a salaried employee who has opted out of the default new regime under section 202 (the HRA exemption is not allowed under it).
Salary includes dearness allowance if provided for under the terms of employment, but excludes all other allowances and perquisites (rule 279(2)(b)).
Rule 279 gives 50% of salary for Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad and Bengaluru; any other place receives 40%.
Assumes the employee actually paid rent for residential accommodation they occupied and do not own during the period.
limitations: The HRA exemption cannot be claimed under the default new regime (section 202(2)(a)(i) of the Income-tax Act, 2025).
Does not calculate month-by-month variances if rent, salary, or city of residence changed during the tax year.
Does not verify landlord PAN requirements that employers apply when annual rent exceeds ₹1,00,000.
Cannot be claimed if the employee lives in their own house or pays no rent.
